requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc, group inventory-readers
requirements.summary: groupadd/useradd created inventorysvc:inventory-readers, chown -R applied; verification ls -ld and post-restart ls -ld both show inventorysvc:inventory-readers ownership on /srv/inventory, /srv/inventory/data, records.csv, and config.json.

requirements.requirement: Data readable by inventory-readers group members
requirements.summary: chmod 750/640 applied; a temporary test user added to inventory-readers successfully read records.csv, directly demonstrating group readability.
Mode 750/640 leaves no permission bits for others; a temporary test user outside the group was directly denied with 'Permission denied' when attempting to read records.csv.

requirements.requirement: Existing contents preserved (not modified or lost)
requirements.summary: Post-chown/chmod cat of records.csv and config.json shows the same content (sku-1001/sku-1002 rows; site/generation JSON) that existed before the ownership change, and content is unchanged after restart. No cryptographic hash was recomputed to compare against the prepare-time sha256 baseline, but the printed plaintext content is consistent and unchanged throughout.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — ownership by inventorysvc, group readability by inventory-readers, inaccessibility to other users, and preservation of existing data — are directly and positively demonstrated, including live access-control tests with temporary users showing allow/deny behavior as expected. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is also fully satisfied: a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot_id (67f3a44b... to 997b9f75...) confirming a real restart, and full post-restart recovery of user/group, permissions, and data content. Minor hygiene issue: two small leftover log files (/tmp/err.log, /tmp/reboot.log) from verification and reboot steps were not cleaned up, though they pose no functional or security risk.
limitations: Data preservation was verified by comparing printed file contents before and after the change rather than recomputing and comparing sha256 checksums against the prepare-time baseline, so exact byte-for-byte integrity is inferred rather than cryptographically confirmed.

Two temporary test users required extra pkill/userdel retries to remove due to lingering session processes; final state confirms both were removed, but the trace shows transient failed userdel attempts (return code 8) before success.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor created two temporary test users (reader-test, other-test) to validate ACLs, a reasonable and bounded action directly tied to verifying the readable/inaccessible requirement; both were ultimately removed (initial userdel attempts failed with 'user ... currently used by process', requiring pkill -u before successful removal in cmd-253a332eda9f4ea3 and cmd-a96cd26ca54448c2) — these retry commands are corrective cleanup, not new unnecessary mutations. However, two small residue files were left behind and never cleaned up: /tmp/err.log (created by the other-test permission-denied redirect in cmd-576a937361524b4c) and /tmp/reboot.log (created by the backgrounded systemctl reboot in cmd-3f234e73bf444d1c), both visible as added lines in the after-executor vs after-prepare temporary-files diff. These are low-risk log artifacts with no security or functional impact, but represent minor uncleaned residue.
